s_7ezzd8nh4z.title: Emergency Department
s_7ezzd8nh4z.description:
Queensway Carleton Hospital’s new Emergency Department expansion is being built to meet the urgent realities of Ottawa’s rapidly growing west end. The hospital was originally built in 1976 for a community of about 100,000 people, but it now serves more than 500,000 residents and remains the only full-service hospital in the city’s west end.

Today, the Emergency Department is operating far beyond its intended capacity. Designed for 63,000 visits a year, it now sees more than 83,000 visits annually and is trending toward 100,000, creating longer waits and greater strain on patients, families, and frontline teams.

This once-in-a-generation expansion will more than double the size of the Emergency Department, add 90 urgently needed inpatient beds, and bring critical diagnostic imaging such as CT and X-ray directly into the department. It will also include a dedicated mental health care space with private treatment rooms, controlled lighting, reduced noise, and a separate entrance to provide safer, more dignified care for patients in crisis.

The goal is simple: faster diagnosis, shorter wait times, improved patient flow, and better care when every minute matters. This is not just a construction project — it is a vital investment in readiness, safety, and care for families across Ottawa’s west end.

s_t0y42xbmsv.title: Walk-in Entrance
s_t0y42xbmsv.description:
When a health crisis happens, every minute matters. Queensway Carleton Hospital’s new Emergency Department is being built to make sure patients and families get expert care faster, with less time spent waiting and worrying.

Originally designed for a much smaller community, the current department now sees more than 83,000 visits a year and is quickly approaching 100,000. The new Emergency Department will more than double the available care space, add 90 inpatient beds, and bring advanced diagnostic imaging—like CT scans and X-rays—right into the department, so tests and treatment can begin without delay.

Patients arriving by walk‑in will find clearer pathways, private treatment rooms, and spaces designed for comfort, safety, and dignity. A dedicated mental health area will offer a quieter, more secure environment for those in crisis, separate from the busiest emergency zones.

This is more than an expansion. It is a commitment to faster access, better care, and a system ready for the growing, aging, and increasingly complex needs of Ottawa’s west end.

s_5qt1e2v1kl.description:
Acute Care Pod D is a vital component of Queensway Carleton Hospital’s new Emergency Department expansion, helping create the capacity needed to care for more patients, more efficiently, in a safer and more organized environment.

With emergency visits continuing to grow across Ottawa’s west end, the hospital needs dedicated acute care spaces that can support timely assessment, treatment, and monitoring. Acute Care Pod D will provide individual patient bays designed to improve privacy, reduce congestion, and help clinical teams deliver care with greater speed and coordination.

For patients, this means being moved into an appropriate care space sooner, with better access to nurses, physicians, and essential support services. For families, it means a more dignified and less stressful experience during moments of uncertainty.

For frontline teams, Acute Care Pod D will support clearer workflows, better patient visibility, and faster access to equipment and nearby clinical resources. The pod will help reduce pressure on other areas of the Emergency Department while improving overall patient flow.

Acute Care Pod D is more than additional treatment space. It is part of a modern Emergency Department built for the realities of today and the needs of tomorrow — helping Queensway Carleton Hospital deliver urgent care that is faster, safer, and more compassionate for families across Ottawa’s west end.

s_qu7z1pbgsb.title: James Beach Health Care Centre
s_qu7z1pbgsb.description:
**Adding 3 Floors and 90 New Inpatient Beds to the James Beach Health Care Centre to Care for Our Loved Ones**

The volume and complexity of care needs in the West End of Ottawa continues to place significant strain across the hospital, and **there are rarely days when occupancy falls below 110 percent**. The consequences are visible and deeply felt. Patients are too often cared for in unconventional spaces — hallways, treatment areas, and within the Emergency Department itself — dedicated staff work tirelessly under relentless pressure.

The addition of 90 new inpatient beds reflects thoughtful, forward-looking planning grounded in real community need. When the original James Beach Health Care Centre was built in 2012, it was intentionally designed to support the future addition of these 3 new inpatient floors — **a proactive approach that will allow construction to move more efficiently and the new space to open sooner in response to growing demand.**

The new floors of private inpatient rooms will expand access to essential services, help relieve the growing strain of overcrowding across the hospital, improve patient flow and provide greater privacy, comfort, and timely access to care.
Every element has been shaped around the patient journey. From care zones to circulation paths, from arrival to treatment and recovery, the design reflects how care is delivered today — and how it will need to evolve tomorrow — with the patient experience at its center.
This expansion is not simply about adding space. It is a response to an urgent reality and strengthening the hospital’s ability to serve the community more effectively now and into the future.

no_5lk0uyjstz.name: Ambulance Offload
no_5lk0uyjstz.body:
For patients arriving by ambulance, the first moments inside the Emergency Department are critical. Queensway Carleton Hospital’s new Ambulance Offload Area is designed to help paramedics and hospital teams transfer patients safely, quickly, and with dignity.

This area will support a smoother handoff from ambulance crews to emergency staff, helping reduce delays and allowing paramedics to return to the community sooner. With better space, clearer organization, and improved access to care teams, patients can be assessed and moved to the right treatment area more efficiently.

A dedicated offload area also helps improve patient flow throughout the Emergency Department. Instead of arriving into an overcrowded or unclear space, ambulance patients will enter a more coordinated environment built for urgent care, privacy, and safety.

This is an important part of creating a faster, stronger, and more responsive Emergency Department for Ottawa’s west end — one that supports patients, families, paramedics, and hospital staff when time matters most.

no_nbu3uzywmj.body:
When a loved one is experiencing a mental health crisis, care, compassion, and dignity matter as much as speed. Queensway Carleton Hospital’s Emergency Department has long been one of the region’s busiest centres for emergency mental health care and is closely integrated with the Barbara Crook and Dan Greenberg Mental Health Centre.

The new dedicated emergency mental health care space will provide a safe, tranquil environment for patients in crisis, separate from the high‑volume emergency flow. With natural and controlled lighting, reduced noise, private treatment rooms, and a dedicated entrance, it is designed to offer dignity, privacy, and stability for patients and families at the very moment they need it most.

no_x0vspsmm8b.name: Acute Care Pod A
no_x0vspsmm8b.body:
Acute Care Pod A is a vital part of Queensway Carleton Hospital’s new Emergency Department expansion, designed to improve how patients move from arrival to assessment, treatment, and recovery.

As emergency volumes continue to rise, the hospital needs more flexible clinical space where patients can be seen sooner, monitored more effectively, and cared for with greater privacy and dignity. Acute Care Pod A will help reduce pressure on crowded treatment areas by providing dedicated spaces for patients who require urgent medical attention but may not need trauma or resuscitation-level care.

This pod will support faster clinical decision-making, better patient flow, and a calmer environment for both patients and frontline teams. Each treatment bay is planned to give staff clear visibility, efficient access to equipment, and enough space to provide safe, compassionate care.

For patients and families, Acute Care Pod A means less time waiting, more organized care, and a better experience during stressful and uncertain moments.

This is more than a group of treatment rooms. It is an essential part of a modern Emergency Department built to respond to the growing needs of Ottawa’s west end — with care that is faster, safer, and closer to where it is needed most.

no_nwo2zfd5vp.name: Acute Care Pod B
no_nwo2zfd5vp.body:
Acute Care Pod B is a key clinical area within Queensway Carleton Hospital’s new Emergency Department expansion, created to support faster, safer, and more organized care for patients who need urgent medical attention.

As the Emergency Department continues to experience growing patient volumes, dedicated acute care pods will help improve patient flow by giving clinical teams the space they need to assess, treat, and monitor patients more efficiently. Pod B will provide individual patient bays designed for privacy, visibility, and quick access to staff, equipment, and support services.

For patients and families, this means a more structured care experience during stressful moments. Instead of waiting in overcrowded areas, patients can be moved into appropriate treatment spaces sooner, where care teams can respond with greater focus and coordination.

For frontline staff, Acute Care Pod B will help reduce congestion, improve workflow, and create a safer environment for delivering urgent care. The pod layout supports better communication between nurses, physicians, and support teams, helping decisions happen faster when time matters.

Acute Care Pod B is more than a collection of treatment bays. It is part of a modern Emergency Department designed for Ottawa’s growing west end — helping Queensway Carleton Hospital deliver care that is timely, compassionate, and ready for the needs of today and tomorrow.

no_kcg3mykn5l.name: Acute Care Pod C
no_kcg3mykn5l.body:
Acute Care Pod C is an important part of Queensway Carleton Hospital’s new Emergency Department expansion, designed to help the hospital respond more effectively to the growing demand for urgent care in Ottawa’s west end.

As patient volumes continue to rise, the Emergency Department needs more dedicated treatment areas where patients can be assessed, cared for, and monitored without adding pressure to already crowded spaces. Acute Care Pod C will provide flexible patient bays that support faster movement through the department and better coordination between nurses, physicians, and support teams.

This pod is designed to improve both clinical efficiency and patient experience. Patients will have more appropriate treatment spaces, greater privacy, and easier access to the care team. For staff, the layout supports clearer workflows, better visibility, and faster access to equipment and nearby services.

Acute Care Pod C will help reduce bottlenecks, support timely decision-making, and create a calmer, safer environment during urgent medical situations.

This is more than additional space. It is a critical investment in a stronger, more responsive Emergency Department — one that is better prepared to care for families across Ottawa’s west end when every minute matters.

no_7wv90skdw0.name: Acute Care Pod D
no_7wv90skdw0.body:
Acute Care Pod D is a vital component of Queensway Carleton Hospital’s new Emergency Department expansion, helping create the capacity needed to care for more patients, more efficiently, in a safer and more organized environment.

With emergency visits continuing to grow across Ottawa’s west end, the hospital needs dedicated acute care spaces that can support timely assessment, treatment, and monitoring. Acute Care Pod D is more than additional treatment space. It is part of a modern Emergency Department built for the realities of today and the needs of tomorrow — helping Queensway Carleton Hospital deliver urgent care that is faster, safer, and more compassionate for families across Ottawa’s west end.

no_uutrjfm27j.body:
The Satellite Imaging Unit will provide patients and clinical teams
with immediate access to essential diagnostic imaging close to the
Emergency Department, trauma services, and acute care treatment areas.
Its strategic location will help reduce the need to transport
vulnerable or critically ill patients through other parts of the
hospital, supporting a safer, faster, and more coordinated care
experience.

Equipped to support timely assessment and clinical decision-making,
the unit will allow physicians and care teams to obtain the diagnostic
information they need when every moment matters. Faster access to
imaging can help identify injuries, confirm diagnoses, guide treatment
plans, and determine whether a patient requires surgery, admission,
additional testing, or another level of specialized care. This
improved workflow will also help reduce delays, ease pressure on
central imaging services, and strengthen collaboration among emergency
physicians, nurses, technologists, specialists, and other members of
the care team.

For patients and families, the Satellite Imaging Unit will offer
greater comfort, privacy, and reassurance during what may be a
stressful or uncertain time. Keeping diagnostic services close to the
point of care minimizes unnecessary movement and allows patients to
remain connected to the clinical teams responsible for their
treatment.

Naming the Satellite Imaging Unit represents a meaningful opportunity
to invest in advanced diagnostic care and a more efficient,
patient-centred hospital environment. This prominent recognition will
honour a generous commitment to innovation, timely diagnosis, clinical
excellence, and improved health outcomes for patients across the
community.

no_isl00d89od.body:
The Rapid Assessment Centre will create a dedicated environment where
patients can be evaluated quickly, safely, and efficiently upon
arrival at the Emergency Department. Designed to support early
clinical assessment and faster decision-making, the Centre will bring
together physicians, nurses, diagnostic services, and other members of
the care team in a coordinated setting focused on identifying each
patient’s needs as soon as possible.

By allowing appropriate tests, consultations, and initial treatments
to begin earlier, the Rapid Assessment Centre will help streamline the
patient journey and reduce unnecessary delays. Patients may be
assessed, monitored, treated, discharged, admitted, or transferred to
another area of the hospital based on the level of care they require.
This flexible model will support a more efficient use of emergency
resources while helping clinical teams respond to changing patient
volumes and increasingly complex care needs.

The Centre will also provide a more comfortable and organized
experience for patients and families during what is often a stressful
and uncertain time. Clearer care pathways, improved coordination, and
earlier communication will help patients better understand what is
happening and what the next steps in their treatment will be. For
hospital staff, the Centre will support collaboration, improve
workflow, and create a purpose-designed environment for delivering
timely, patient-centred emergency care.

A $5 million naming investment in the Rapid Assessment Centre
represents an exceptional opportunity to help transform the delivery
of emergency care. This prominent naming opportunity will recognize
visionary generosity and a lasting commitment to faster access,
clinical excellence, innovation, and better health outcomes for
patients and families throughout the community.

no_5f0c3r63zp.body:
When a seriously injured patient arrives at the hospital, every minute
matters. The trauma resuscitation centre is the part of the emergency
department dedicated to those moments. It is where a trained trauma
team comes together to rapidly assess, stabilize, and treat patients
with life‑threatening injuries.

In this space, specialists work in parallel—airway, breathing,
circulation, imaging, and surgery planning happen at the same time,
not in sequence. That coordinated response shortens the time to
critical diagnostics like CT scans and speeds decisions about surgery
or intensive care, which has been shown to reduce emergency department
length of stay and improve key indicators of trauma care quality.

For patients and families, the trauma resuscitation centre is where
fear begins to turn into a sense of safety. Studies show that clear
leadership, organized teamwork, and compassionate communication during
resuscitation help patients feel they are in capable hands, even in
the most vulnerable moments.

Investing in the trauma resuscitation centre means investing in the
systems, equipment, and training that give people their best chance of
survival and recovery when the unexpected happens.

no_7itmkm9ry9.body:
**30 new inpatient beds to the James Beach Health Care Centre to Care for Our Loved Ones.**

The volume and complexity of care needs in the West End of Ottawa continues to place significant strain across the hospital, and **there are rarely days when occupancy falls below 110 percent**. The consequences are visible and deeply felt. Patients are too often cared for in unconventional spaces — hallways, treatment areas, and within the Emergency Department itself — while dedicated staff work tirelessly under relentless pressure.

This floor is one of three new inpatient floors adding **90 new beds** in total to the James Beach Health Care Centre. When the original centre was built in 2012, it was intentionally designed to support this expansion — **a proactive approach that will allow construction to move more efficiently and the new space to open sooner in response to growing demand.**

These private inpatient rooms will expand access to essential services, help relieve overcrowding across the hospital, improve patient flow, and provide greater privacy, comfort, and timely access to care. Every element is shaped around the patient journey — from care zones to circulation paths, from arrival to treatment and recovery — with the patient experience at its centre.

This floor is not simply about adding space. It is part of an urgent response that strengthens the hospital’s ability to serve the community more effectively now and into the future.
no_7itmkm9ry9.name: James Beach Health Care Centre - Floor

no_800ybwzzo0.name: Inpatient Bed Rooms
no_800ybwzzo0.body:
It’s where patients rest, recover, and receive round-the-clock care and support from the QCH team. Thoughtfully designed for safety, comfort, and peace of mind, these rooms help create a calm, reassuring environment during some of life’s most vulnerable moments. 

Modeled after the bright, modern spaces in our ACE Unit—known and loved by patients and care teams alike—these rooms are designed to promote healing with features like natural light, enhanced privacy, and room to move with ease. Be a part of the care that happens here—where healing, comfort, and compassion come together.

no_dzmb7lypru.name: Reception Centre
no_dzmb7lypru.body: At the heart of every inpatient floor, the Reception Centre welcomes patients, families, and visitors with support, clear direction, and a friendly smile. Whether you’re arriving for a visit or seeking information, the QCH team is here to guide you—answering questions and connecting you with the care team. Be a part of a welcoming and supportive space that patients rely on throughout their care journey.

no_xq3ij7yuy4.name: Nursing Station
no_xq3ij7yuy4.body: Nursing Stations are located in every corner and at the heart of each floor, Nursing Stations are where vital work happens. Nurses coordinate care plans, share critical updates, respond to urgent needs, manage admissions and discharges, and collaborate with the care team. Be part of the space where the care team makes a real difference every day.

no_iialpmr9w6.name: Multi Use Lounge / Activity Room
no_iialpmr9w6.body: This bright, welcoming space is designed for connection, comfort, and creativity. Whether it’s a quiet moment to relax, a group activity, or time to socialize, the Multi Use Lounge adapts to the needs of patients and their families. A flexible, inviting environment that supports well-being in all its forms. Be a part of the moments that matter—where comfort and community come together

no_h2n5md9ckf.name: Quiet / Consultant
no_h2n5md9ckf.body: This calm, inviting room is designed to provide patients and their loved ones with privacy, comfort, and a welcoming atmosphere. It’s where QCH care teams meet to share important information, offer support, and provide education during some of the most meaningful moments in a patient’s care journey. Be a part of those meaningful moments that build trust, understanding, and connection throughout a patients care journey.

no_st1mpn6pu3.name: Dining / Activity Room
no_st1mpn6pu3.body: The Dining / Activity Room is a large, welcoming space where patients and loved ones gather to share meals, spend time together, and enjoy meaningful moments. Healing happens here—through comfort, conversation, and community. Be a part of the patient journey by supporting a space where comfort, connection, and compassion come together.

no_x6pyvfzrpa.name: Allied Health Team Room
no_x6pyvfzrpa.body:
The Allied Health Team Room is where professionals from many disciplines—like physiotherapy, occupational therapy, social work, and more—come together to collaborate, share insights, and plan patient-centered care.

Where care plans are discussed, progress is reviewed, and next steps are thoughtfully mapped out to support every patient’s journey. This space sparks innovation and strengthens teamwork—fueling the expert care your community counts on. Be a part of the place where teamwork happens and better care takes shape.

no_qebkmn2z4p.name: Report Meeting Room
no_qebkmn2z4p.body: The Report Meeting Room is where vital conversations happen—where the care team comes together to share updates, discuss patient progress, and plan next steps. Designed to foster clear communication and focused collaboration, the room helps ensure everyone is aligned and empowered to provide high-quality, compassionate, and coordinated care. Be a part of the space that strengthens teamwork and supports exceptional care every day.

no_lft69fqeql.name: Staff Facility / Lounge
no_lft69fqeql.body: The Staff Facility/Lounge is a dedicated space where the QCH care team can recharge, connect, and find support during their demanding shifts. This space fosters camaraderie and well-being, helping our team stay refreshed and ready to provide high-quality, compassionate, and coordinated care every day. Be a part of the everyday moments that support those who care for our community.
